basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 28.' and it opens 'Vers. 28. Hebdomada transacta. Non est putandum quod post septem annos servitutis Rachel'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 28. Hebdomada transacta. Non est putandum quod post septem annos servitutis Rachel duxerit uxorem, sed impletis septem diebus post nuptias Liae, quibus impletis servivit septem annis.
